text: Before we begin, let us clear our minds of distractions and make room for prayer. We turn our attention to Jesus, with Mary. Sit comfortably. Breathe gently, without straining. Let us take four gentle, comfortable breaths together.
Breathe in gently.
And breathe out slowly.
Breathe in gently.
And breathe out slowly.
Breathe in gently.
And breathe out slowly.
Breathe in gently.
And breathe out slowly.
Let us pray together. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

I believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried; he descended into hell; on the third day he rose again from the dead; he ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty; from there he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting. Amen.

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
For an increase in faith.

Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
For an increase in hope.

The first Sorrowful Mystery. The Agony in the Garden. The fruit of this mystery is faithfulness to the Father's will.

Jesus prays in the garden with sorrow unto death. He asks that the cup pass, yet submits fully: "Nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt." He finds the disciples sleeping and calls them to watch and pray. He accepts the Passion in perfect trust.

In Gethsemane, Jesus embraces the Father's will in agony, teaching obedience under suffering.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.
Picture Jesus entering Gethsemane after the Last Supper.
Picture Jesus asking His disciples to remain with Him and pray.
Picture the disciples sleeping while Jesus carries His sorrow alone.
Picture Jesus praying to the Father about the cup before Him.
Picture Jesus surrendering His will to the Father.

Ask Christ for faithfulness to the Father's will.

Picture Jesus praying in anguish, His sweat like drops of blood.
Picture the angel strengthening Jesus.
Picture Jesus continuing in prayer in the dark garden.
Picture Jesus rising and returning to His disciples.
Picture Jesus facing the approaching crowd without turning away.

The second Sorrowful Mystery. The Scourging at the Pillar. The fruit of this mystery is purity of heart.

Jesus is brought before Pilate, questioned, and rejected by the crowd. Though innocent, He is handed over and scourged. The scene shows injustice, violence, and Christ's silent endurance for the salvation of souls.

The Scourging reveals Christ's innocent suffering and the cost of human sin.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.
Picture Jesus standing innocent before those who condemn Him.
Picture Jesus bound at the pillar.
Picture Jesus turning His heart to the Father in prayer.
Picture Jesus remaining silent through humiliation and pain.
Picture Christ enduring the suffering without abandoning His love.
Ask Christ for purity of heart. Picture His steadfast love for every person.
Picture His bound hands remaining still.
Picture Jesus remaining faithful to the Father, even when others are unkind.
Picture the love of Jesus reaching you in your own difficulties.
Picture Jesus being led away from the pillar.

The third Sorrowful Mystery. The Crowning with Thorns. The fruit of this mystery is moral courage and humility.

Pilate offers release, but the crowd chooses Barabbas. Soldiers clothe Jesus in purple, press thorns on His head, strike and mock Him, and lead Him to crucifixion. The true King accepts humiliation without hatred.

The Crowning with Thorns reveals mocked kingship: Christ reigns through truth, humility, and love.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.
Picture the soldiers gathering around Jesus to mock Him.
Picture Jesus, the humble King, answering cruelty with patient love.
Picture Jesus hearing their ridicule without answering in anger.
Picture the reed in His hand and the robe upon His shoulders.
Picture the true King standing before those who mock Him.

Ask Christ for moral courage and humility.

Picture Jesus remaining gentle amid their cruelty.
Picture His face beneath the crown of thorns.
Picture the soldiers bowing in mock homage.
Picture Jesus bearing their contempt in silence.
Picture Christ standing wounded, yet faithful to the Father's love.

The fourth Sorrowful Mystery. The Carrying of the Cross. The fruit of this mystery is patience and faithful endurance.

Pilate yields to pressure and delivers Jesus to be crucified. Jesus carries the Cross; Simon of Cyrene is compelled to help. Women mourn as Jesus speaks to them with prophetic compassion. The road of suffering becomes the road of redemption.

On the way to Calvary, Christ carries the Cross and invites discipleship through endurance.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.
Picture Jesus beginning the road to Calvary, trusting the Father.
Picture the dusty road toward Calvary and the crowd around Him.
The Stations of the Cross traditionally invite us to remember Jesus falling and rising again. Picture His patient courage on the road.
The Stations of the Cross traditionally invite us to remember Mary meeting Jesus. Picture their loving gaze along the road.
Picture Simon helping Jesus carry the cross.

Ask Christ for patience and faithful endurance.

In the traditional Way of the Cross, picture Veronica offering compassion to Jesus.
Picture Jesus moving forward beneath the weight of the wood.
Picture Simon remaining beside Him on the difficult road.
Picture Mary continuing along the path toward Calvary.
Picture Jesus reaching the place where He will be crucified.

The fifth Sorrowful Mystery. The Crucifixion. The fruit of this mystery is self-giving love and repentance.

Jesus is crucified between two criminals. He is mocked, yet forgives and promises paradise to the repentant thief. Darkness falls; then Jesus cries out, "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit." Then He dies. The centurion recognizes His innocence.

At Calvary, Jesus offers His life completely and opens mercy even at the hour of death.

Stay with this mystery as you pray.
Picture Mary and the beloved disciple remaining near Jesus at the Cross.
Picture Jesus praying for the forgiveness of those who crucify Him.
Picture Jesus entrusting Mary and the beloved disciple to each other.
Picture Jesus thirsting as darkness surrounds the Cross.
Picture the repentant thief turning toward Jesus and receiving His promise.

Ask Christ for self-giving love and repentance.

Picture Jesus declaring that His work is finished.
Picture Jesus bowing His head and giving up His spirit.
Picture Mary remaining at the foot of the Cross.
Picture the silence around the Cross after Jesus dies.
Picture those who love Him staying near His body.

Hail, Holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness, and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us, and after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.
Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
Let us pray.

O God, whose Only Begotten Son, by his life, Death, and Resurrection, has purchased for us the rewards of eternal life, grant, we beseech thee, that while meditating on these mysteries of the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise, through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
